requirements.requirement: Healthy 3-member etcd cluster running across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys (baseline before disruption)
requirements.summary: member list shows all three nodes 'started'; endpoint health shows 3/3 true; application keys written on node1 and confirmed readable from node2 and node3, directly demonstrating the pre-disruption healthy baseline.

requirements.requirement: node3 member permanently lost with data unrecoverable, cluster retains quorum during the disruption
requirements.summary: node3 etcd was stopped, disabled, and its data directory wiped; a subsequent cluster health check directly shows node3's endpoint failing (context deadline exceeded) while node1 and node2 remain healthy, demonstrating quorum was preserved during the bounded disruption.

requirements.requirement: Dead node3 member removed and replaced with a new working member on the same system, cluster restored to 3 healthy members
requirements.summary: Old member ID was removed via etcdctl member remove, a new member was added with existing-cluster state, etcd started successfully on node3, and immediately-following member list/endpoint health output directly shows 3/3 healthy members including the new node3 identity.

requirements.requirement: Existing application keys remain intact after the member replacement
requirements.summary: A direct etcdctl get against the new node3 member returns all three original application keys with correct values, confirming raft resync restored data without loss.

overall_summary: The executor bootstrapped a fresh 3-member etcd cluster (none pre-existed), loaded it with application keys, directly demonstrated a healthy baseline, simulated node3's permanent unrecoverable loss while node1/node2 retained quorum, removed the dead member and added a new working member on node3, and confirmed the cluster returned to 3/3 healthy members with all original keys intact via a direct etcdctl get on the new member. All material task outcomes are supported by direct before/during/after command evidence rather than configuration alone. The separately mandated per-node restart protocol was also executed for all three nodes with matching pre/post boot-id evidence that is consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-restart checks confirm recovered cluster/member/key state each time.
limitations: The environment was greenfield (no etcd pre-existed), so the 'permanent loss' of node3 was simulated by the executor itself rather than being an externally injected fault; this is a reasonable and necessary way to fulfill the task contract in this environment but means the failure scenario is self-manufactured rather than independently observed.
Leftover installation artifacts (etcd tarball and extracted directory) remain in /tmp on all three nodes; low-risk but not cleaned up.

Command cmd-9392cee6cd7144f9 (initial etcd start on node1) returned a non-zero exit due to a timeout; state was verified healthy shortly after, but the trace does not fully explain the root cause of that transient failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were consistently tied to task purposes: installing etcd, opening firewall ports, bootstrapping the cluster, simulating node3's permanent loss (necessary since no etcd pre-existed and the scenario had to be manufactured), replacing the member, and performing the mandated per-node restart protocol. One state-changing command (cmd-9392cee6cd7144f9, node1's first 'systemctl enable --now etcd') returned a timeout failure but is a transient bootstrap race (peers not yet up) rather than a harmful mutation, and the service was subsequently confirmed active (cmd-b71bc3872b224f3b) with no lasting damage. The one avoidable hygiene issue is that the etcd release tarball and extracted directory (/tmp/etcd.tar.gz, /tmp/etcd-v3.7.1-linux-amd64/*) downloaded during installation (cmd-54e974e9f9264baa, cmd-fa9a073daa784890, cmd-d21b1eb8ac3b44be) were left behind on all three nodes and are visible as residue in the after-executor temporary-files snapshots; this is bounded, low-risk, non-destructive leftover but was never cleaned up.
